title: IO submission record
description: Language-neutral description of an async I/O request submitted by the storage layer to the I/O backend. The backend accepts a queue of these records and emits io-completion records in response. No language-specific idioms (pointers, lifetimes, Result types) appear in this schema; each generator maps the record to an idiomatic in-memory shape in its target language.

op.description: Operation kind. The backend dispatches by this tag.

user_data.description: Opaque token chosen by the submitter. The backend MUST echo it verbatim in the matching completion record. Encoded as an unsigned 64-bit integer; generators MAY narrow to a smaller int if the deployment cannot overflow.

epoch.description: Monotonic session-epoch counter. Completions whose epoch is LESS than the current pager epoch MUST be dropped silently (they refer to a cancelled transaction or closed handle). See pager-async.spec.md § 'Cancellation semantics'.

handle.description: Opaque file handle identifier. Required for: read, write, fsync, fsync_dir, close. Omitted for open_read, open_write, rename, unlink, cancel. Generators map this to a file descriptor (C), file object (Rust), or JS host handle (WASM).

path.description: Filesystem path, UTF-8. Required for: open_read, open_write, rename (source), unlink, fsync_dir. Omitted otherwise.

new_path.description: Destination path for rename. Required only when op == 'rename'.

create.description: Create file if absent. Applies to op == 'open_write' only.

truncate.description: Truncate existing file to zero on open. Applies to op == 'open_write' only.

offset.description: Byte offset in the file. Required for read and write.

length.description: Byte count. Required for read and write. MUST equal the payload_buffer's capacity for a read and the payload_buffer's byte length for a write.

payload_buffer_ref.description: Identifier of a backend-owned or submitter-owned buffer holding (for write) or receiving (for read) the bytes. The spec treats this as an opaque token; each generator binds it to a native buffer primitive (C: pointer + length; Rust: &mut [u8] or indexed buffer pool slot; WASM: memory region index). Lifecycle: caller guarantees the buffer is live from submission until the matching completion record is observed. Omitted for fsync, fsync_dir, close, rename, unlink, cancel.

cancel_target.description: user_data of the submission to cancel. Required only when op == 'cancel'. If no in-flight submission carries this user_data, the cancel op completes with result_bytes = 0 and no error (idempotent).

datasync.description: Hint: data-only durability is sufficient (metadata need not be flushed). Applies to op == 'fsync'. Backends MAY ignore the hint. On Darwin, backends MUST NOT honour this hint — F_FULLFSYNC is required for crash durability regardless.

link_prior.description: Ordering hint: this submission MUST complete only after the most recently submitted operation on the same handle. Backends use this to chain dependent ops (e.g., write-then-fsync). A backend MAY preserve same-handle order unconditionally and ignore the hint.
